cards.heading: Console
cards.body: The console port gives out-of-band access with a rollover/USB cable, even when the network is down. It's the first way into a new device.

cards.heading: Telnet and SSH
cards.body: Remote CLI access goes through the VTY lines. Telnet (TCP 23) sends everything, including passwords, in clear text. SSH (TCP 22) encrypts the session; always use SSH and restrict the VTY lines to it.
cards.example:
line vty 0 4
 login local
 transport input ssh

cards.heading: HTTP and HTTPS
cards.body: Many devices, especially WLCs, offer a web GUI. HTTP (TCP 80) is clear text; HTTPS (TCP 443) is encrypted. Disable plain HTTP: 'no ip http server', 'ip http secure-server'.

cards.heading: Centralised authentication
cards.body: Instead of local accounts on every device, AAA servers check logins centrally. TACACS+ (Cisco, TCP 49) encrypts the whole payload and separates authorisation, so it suits device administration. RADIUS (UDP 1812/1813) suits network access such as Wi-Fi and 802.1X.

cards.heading: In-band, out-of-band and cloud
cards.body: In-band management uses the production network (SSH to an SVI). Out-of-band uses a separate path such as the console or a dedicated management port and network, so it works during outages. Cloud-managed devices are configured from a vendor dashboard.

cards.heading: Managing a layer 2 switch
cards.body: A layer 2 switch has no routed ports, so it gets its management address on an SVI in the management VLAN. To be reachable from other subnets it also needs 'ip default-gateway', because it doesn't route.
cards.example:
interface vlan 99
 ip address 10.99.0.11 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
!
ip default-gateway 10.99.0.1
